Below is a **7‑day “Paris in a Week” travel plan** that balances the classic sights with some off‑the‑beaten‑path experiences. Feel free to tweak the dates, budget, or activities to match your own interests and travel style. --- ## 1️⃣ Pre‑Trip Checklist | Item | Why It Matters | Tips | |------|----------------|------| | **Passport & Visa** | Must be valid for at least 6 months. EU/US/Canada/UK passports usually don’t need a visa for stays <90 days. | Check the French consulate website for your country. | | **Travel Insurance** | Covers medical, trip cancellation, lost luggage. | Look for “European coverage” and “24/7 assistance.” | | **Flight Booking** | Book 2–3 months ahead for best fares. | Use fare alerts (Google Flights, Skyscanner). | | **Accommodation** | Central location saves time & money on transport. | Consider a boutique hotel, Airbnb, or a 3‑star hotel in the 1st–7th arrondissements. | | **SIM Card / Roaming** | Stay connected & use navigation. | Buy a local SIM (Orange, SFR) or use a global plan. | | **Packing** | Weather in Paris is mild; layers are key. | Pack a lightweight rain jacket, comfortable walking shoes, a scarf, and a small day‑pack. | | **Currency** | Euro (€). | Have some cash for small cafés; most places accept cards. | --- ## 2️⃣ Flights & Arrival | Day | Activity | Notes | |-----|----------|-------| | **Day 0** | Fly into Paris‑Charles de Gaulle (CDG) or Orly (ORY). | Arrive early morning or late night to maximize Day 1. | | | Transfer to hotel | • **RER B** from CDG → Saint‑Germain‑en‑Laye → **Hotel** (if in 1st–7th arr.)
• **Orlyval** + **RER B** from ORY
• Taxi or rideshare (approx €35–€45). | | | Check‑in & rest | Take a short walk around your neighborhood to orient yourself. | --- ## 3️⃣ 7‑Day Itinerary > **Tip:** Buy a **Paris Pass** (includes metro, major attractions, and a hop‑on hop‑off bus) or a **Navigo Week Pass** (unlimited metro/bus) for €30–€40. | Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening | |-----|---------|-----------|---------| | **1** | **Notre‑Dame & Île de la Cité** – walk the cathedral, read the gargoyles. | **Sainte‑Chapelle** (book tickets in advance). | **Latin Quarter** – dinner at a bistro, stroll along the Seine. | | **2** | **Louvre Museum** – start early, focus on the Mona Lisa & Venus de Milo. | **Tuileries Garden** – relax, maybe a coffee at Angelina. | **Champs‑Élysées** – light show at Arc de Triomphe, dinner near the Arc. | | **3** | **Eiffel Tower** – book a skip‑the‑line ticket. | **Champ de Mars** picnic (grab baguette, cheese, wine). | **Seine River Cruise** (night cruise shows illuminated landmarks). | | **4** | **Montmartre** – Sacré‑Coeur, artists’ square, hidden passages. | **Place du Tertre** – get a portrait. | **Moulin Rouge** show (or a jazz club in Pigalle). | | **5** | **Versailles** – day trip (RER C). | Explore the palace, gardens, and the Trianon. | Return to Paris, dinner in the Marais. | | **6** | **Musée d’Orsay** – Impressionist masterpieces. | **Le Marais** – boutique shopping, falafel at L’As du Fallafel. | **Seine-side walk** – sunset at Pont Alexandre III. | | **7** | **Picnic at Parc des Buttes‑Chaumont** or **Luxembourg Gardens**. | **Shopping** – Galeries Lafayette, Printemps. | **Farewell dinner** – try a classic French restaurant (e.g., Le Comptoir du Relais). | --- ## 4️⃣ Optional Day Trips (swap any day) | Destination | How to Get There | Highlights | |-------------|-----------------|------------| | **Giverny** | Train to Vernon (RER C) → bus to Giverny. | Monet’s house & gardens. | | **Fontaine‑bleau** | Train from Paris (RER C). | Château, park, and the Musée de l’Île. | | **Château de Fontainebleau** | Same as above. | Renaissance architecture, forest walks. | | **Disneyland Paris** | RER A to Marne‑la‑Vallee. | Theme park fun (great for families). | --- ## 5️⃣ Dining & Food Highlights | Category | Recommendation | Why | |----------|----------------|-----| | **Breakfast** | **Café de Flore** or **Le Pain Quotidien** | Classic croissants & coffee. | | **Lunch** | **L’As du Fallafel** (Marais) | Legendary falafel. | | **Dinner** | **Le Comptoir du Relais** (Saint‑Germain) | Intimate bistro, seasonal menu. | | **Dessert** | **Pierre Hermé** (multiple locations) | World‑famous macarons. | | **Wine** | **La Cave à Michel** (Le Marais) | Small, curated selection. | | **Cheese** | **Fromagerie Laurent Dubois** | Try Camembert, Roquefort, Brie. | --- ## 6️⃣ Budget Breakdown (per person, 7 days) | Category | Approx. Cost (€) | |----------|------------------| | **Flights** | 200–600 (depending on origin & season) | | **Accommodation** | 80–200/night (mid‑range) → 560–1400 | | **Transport (Paris Pass + day trips)** | 120–200 | | **Food** | 30–50/day → 210–350 | | **Attractions** | 100–200 (skip‑the‑line tickets, museums) | | **Misc. (souvenirs, tips)** | 50–100 | | **Total** | **≈ 1,200–2,500** | *(Prices are estimates; adjust based on your travel style.)* --- ## 7️⃣ Tips & Hacks | Tip | How It Helps | |-----|--------------| | **Buy tickets online** | Skip long queues at Louvre, Eiffel Tower, Versailles. | | **Use the Metro** | Fast, cheap, and covers most attractions. | | **Walk whenever possible** | Paris is very walkable; you’ll discover hidden cafés. | | **Eat at lunch** | Many restaurants offer a “menu du jour” (~€12–€18) – great value. | | **Stay central** | Saves on transport time; you’ll be within 15‑20 min of most sights. | | **Check opening hours** | Some museums close on Mondays; plan accordingly. | | **Pack a reusable water bottle** | Tap water is safe and free. | | **Learn basic French phrases** | “Bonjour”, “Merci”, “Où est…?” – locals appreciate the effort. | --- ## 8️⃣ Sample Packing List | Category | Items | |----------|-------| | **Clothing** | 3‑4 tops, 2‑3 bottoms, light jacket, raincoat, comfortable walking shoes, dressy outfit for dinner. | | **Accessories** | Scarf, sunglasses, hat, small day‑pack, reusable water bottle. | | **Electronics** | Phone, charger, power bank, adapter (Type C/E). | | **Documents** | Passport, visa (if needed), travel insurance, flight tickets, hotel confirmation, copies of reservations. | | **Health** | Prescription meds, basic first aid kit, hand sanitizer, face masks (if desired). | --- ### Final Thought Paris is a city that rewards curiosity. Even if you stick to the classic itinerary, you’ll find countless cafés, street performers, and hidden gardens that make the experience uniquely yours. Enjoy the art, the food, the history, and the effortless charm of the City of Light! 🌟 Let me know if you’d like a more tailored plan (e.g., budget, dates, interests) or help with booking details. Bon voyage!
